summary_en: GMO Pepabo will conduct a single stock transfer to establish holding company GMO AI Commerce Holdings effective April 1, 2027, with delisting from TSE Standard Market on March 30, 2027, and technical listing of the new holding company on the same market on April 1, 2027. Concurrently, the holding company will pursue complete acquisition of GMO Make Shop through stock swap with parent company GMO Internet Group.
title_en: Notice of Intention to Transition to Holding Company Structure through Single Stock Transfer and to Initiate Discussions on Complete Acquisition of GMO Make Shop Co., Ltd. by the Holding Company
translation_en_brief:
GMO Pepabo announced on November 13, 2026, that its board of directors has resolved to transition to a holding company structure through a single stock transfer effective April 1, 2027. Under this reorganization, the company will establish a new holding company named GMO AI Commerce Holdings through the stock transfer, with GMO Pepabo becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary. GMO Pepabo will delist from the Tokyo Stock Exchange Standard Market on March 30, 2027, but the newly established holding company will apply for a technical listing on the same market, with listing expected on April 1, 2027.

The stock transfer is conditional upon approval from an extraordinary shareholders meeting scheduled for January 19, 2027, and completion of required procedures. The company states that the transition to a holding company structure aims to strengthen strategic management functions for the entire group, accelerate decision-making and autonomous growth in individual operating divisions through delegation of authority, expand the business portfolio strategically within the commerce and related domains, and enhance governance by separating management oversight from operational execution.

Simultaneously, GMO Pepabo's board has resolved to initiate discussions with the parent company GMO Internet Group and GMO Make Shop regarding a stock swap to make GMO Make Shop—currently a subsidiary of GMO Internet Group—a wholly-owned subsidiary of the new holding company. This proposed merger is expected to constitute a related-party transaction with the controlling shareholder and represents the first step toward creating a leading domestic e-commerce platform group.
